_comment: Template config for the sdlc-pipeline skill. Copy this into the repo you want to drive as `sdlc-pipeline.config.json` (or `.claude/sdlc-pipeline.config.json`) and replace every value below. The skill itself is generic and ships no real config. Despite the `projectFields` name, none of this is a GitHub Projects-v2 board field -- every id here is one of GitHub's ORG-LEVEL custom Issue Types/Issue Fields (the same family: Settings -> Issue types / Issue fields for your org), automatically available on every repo in the org once created, no Projects-v2 board required at all. Look every id up once via `gh api graphql` introspection. See README.md.

pipeline._comment: Optional. Every key below is shown at its default; omit any you don't need to change. `python3 sdlc_next.py show-config` prints the effective values.

locks._comment: Per-branch flock every branch-writing command takes; `{worktreesRoot}` expands to worktrees.root. SDLC_LOCK_DIR in the environment overrides `dir`.

skill._comment: Where this repo vendors the skill as a submodule. worktree-add/sync-branch run `git submodule update --init` on it inside each unit's worktree so agents read the branch's own pinned copy. Empty submodulePath disables.

stack._comment: Per-epic isolated runtime stack (provision-epic-stack / teardown-epic-stack). Config-only isolation: your compose must read COMPOSE_PROJECT_NAME, every key under `ports`, and `dataDirKey`. Placeholders: {profile} {n} {project} {envFile} {secretsFile} {dataDir} {workspaceRoot}.

gates._comment: Global gate defaults; a profile's own `gates` override these for epics that match it.

productWip._comment: Repo-wide cap on units sitting at Stage=Product with an open Gate A (awaiting-human-review / feedback-received). next-action and list-design-ready stop starting fresh product delegations at the cap; 0 disables.

workItemProvider._comment: V2 (2026-09-14): which WorkItemProvider get_work_item_provider() returns. Only "github" is implemented -- Jira is a documented seam (README.md, "V2: Initiative-driven lifecycle"), not built. Naming anything else is a refusal, not a silent fallback.

pipeline._classification_comment: V2: how GitHub.classify_unit tells an Initiative from an Epic from a Task. Defaults here to LABELS, not Issue Types: custom Issue Types are an organization-level GitHub feature (as of 2026) and are not available on a personal (non-org) repo at any plan tier, while labels work identically everywhere -- create the three labels below in your repo and this works with zero further setup. If your repo IS in an org and you'd rather use real Issue Types (Initiative/Epic provisioned as custom types), swap each rule's "field" to "issueType" and "value" to the type's exact name, and add matching entries to projectFields.issueTypeIds above so set_issue_type can write them back. classify_unit returns "other", never a guess, for any issue matching none of these.

profiles._comment: Ordered; the first whose `match` label is on the epic wins, `"*"` is the catch-all. A profile bundles the behaviour that used to be hardcoded to epic:standing/epic:legacy. Missing toggles inherit the shipped defaults; `gates` inherit the global `gates` above.
profiles.name: legacy

gates._comment: A standing/RTB backlog: lower the Gate B skip bar and let children through Gate A without a human.
